subject.title: fix(tui): run new sessions through lifecycle hooks

question: Should TUI `/new` now create persisted backend sessions through the shared Gateway lifecycle and reject rollover while the parent session is active or admitted?
rationale: The branch is the clean fix for the documented hook regression, but it intentionally changes observable TUI session-state behavior during active or finishing runs.

options.title: Accept shared lifecycle behavior
options.body: Land this PR after normal checks because it restores documented hook/session-memory semantics while preserving isolated TUI sessions.

options.title: Require a compatibility carve-out
options.body: Ask for a narrower patch if the old local empty-session rollover must remain available while hooks are restored another way.

recommendation.title: Accept shared lifecycle behavior
recommendation.body: Land this PR after normal checks because it restores documented hook/session-memory semantics while preserving isolated TUI sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored this repair and are tied to the prior TUI `/new` isolation landing history, so they are the best available owner for the session-state tradeoff.
